newsitem.title: UK: Horlick says had "informal" talks with ABN AMRO.
newsitem.headline: Horlick says had "informal" talks with ABN AMRO.

text.p: Former Morgan Grenfell fund manager Nicola Horlick said on Wedneday that she had been in talks with rival firm ABN AMRO until several days before she was suspended.
But she said the talks were of an "informal and preliminary nature" and that at no stage did she provide ABN AMRO with confidential information about the business or colleagues.
"The talks terminated several days before I was suspended," said Horlick. "My aim was always to keep the clients and the team together for the benefit of all."

Horlick is campaigning to be reinstated or compensated by Morgan Grenfell Asset Management (MGAM) after resigning last week amid allegations she planned to defect to ABN AMRO and was soliciting MGAM colleagues to go with her.
The 35 year-old Horlick has been in talks with her lawyers for the past few days and is considering taking legal action against her former employer for constructive dismissal.
MGAM has repeatedly said it will not reinsate Horlick nor offer compensation as she had resigned her position.
She was suspended last week just days after being promoted to be managing director of MGAM. ABN AMRO has denied trying to poach Horlick and her team.
